title: Surreal Numbers (opening chapters)
note: This PDF holds the first four chapters of Knuth’s novelette. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: Two ex-students on a remote beach dig up a stone carved with Conway’s rules for creating numbers, told like a creation story. Working it out together, they rebuild the theory of surreal numbers from two rules: a number is a pair of sets of earlier numbers, left and right, with nothing on the left at least anything on the right; and an order relation defined recursively in terms of those sets. The real subject is how mathematics is done: translating words into symbols, testing conjectures on small cases, generalizing, and finding a proof by trying to disprove a claim.

chapters.title: 1. The Rock
chapters.summary: Bill and Alice, months into living off the grid, find a buried stone whose inscription describes Conway creating zero from two empty sets, then one and minus one.

chapters.title: 2. Symbols
chapters.summary: Alice rewrites the stone’s rules in symbols: a number is a pair of sets (left, right), and ≤ is defined recursively. They check why the empty-set cases make sense.

chapters.title: 3. Proofs
chapters.summary: They suspect the stone’s “equal” means something weaker, “like”, and start proving small facts about the order, then see a general pattern that covers infinitely many cases.

chapters.title: 4. Bad Numbers
chapters.summary: Counting the numbers born on the third day leads them to need transitivity. Trying to disprove it with “bad” triples of numbers, they find that each bad triple yields a simpler one, which is impossible, and so prove the law.
